purpose: Regional pressure-interference screening; not calibrated for engineering design, seismic-risk assessment or permitting.

boundary_conditions.lateral: Four MULTIPLY operations apply a 1,000,000 pore-volume multiplier to the west, east, south and north edge-cell sets. Corner cells are included in two edge operations and therefore receive the multiplier twice. This is a large-volume pressure-sink approximation rather than an explicit aquifer or fixed-pressure boundary.

faults.representation: Supplied map traces rasterized to MULTX and MULTY faces and extended vertically through all six layers.
faults.shared_state_rule: Every fault uses the same selected state in a scenario.

schedule.browser_after_year_20: The final year-20 response is held constant; years 21-60 are not separately simulated post-injection states.

browser_combination_method: Alpha is scaled by its selected rate. Beta and Zeta use the incremental difference between their two-well unit response and the Alpha-only response, scaled linearly by the selected rate.
limitations: The current OPM grid is flat and homogeneous within each realization; mapped geological surfaces and cell-scale properties are visual context only.
The lateral boundary treatment is a screening approximation and has not been calibrated to regional aquifer support.
No coupled geomechanics, thermal coupling, stress-dependent fault behaviour or induced-seismicity probability is simulated.
The interface pressure constraint is user-configured and is not a calibrated fracture-pressure or fault-reactivation threshold.
Multi-project controls use linear unit-response superposition rather than a new fully coupled OPM run.
The OPM schedule ends at year 20. Later interface years hold the final simulated response and do not represent modeled pressure dissipation.
